concepts.title: Nature's Treasures: Air and Water
concepts.definition: Fresh air and clear water top the list of nature's treasures: air fills every breath and fans every flame, and water, drawn from rivers, rain and groundwater, serves drinking, farming and industry.
concepts.key_idea: The free gifts, air and water, are the most valuable: life stops within minutes or days without them.

concepts.title: Forests: The Green Treasury
concepts.definition: Forests shelter countless plants, animals and birds, hold soil against rain, feed rivers, and give timber, fruits, honey and medicines; the Western Ghats village of the chapter lives beside this green wealth.
concepts.key_idea: A forest is a living bank: it stores water, soil, oxygen and species for every generation.

concepts.title: Soil, Rocks and Fossil Fuels
concepts.definition: Beneath our feet lie more treasures: soil that grows our food, rocks and minerals that build and power our homes, and fossil fuels, coal, petrol and natural gas, stores of ancient energy formed over millions of years.
concepts.key_idea: The earth's crust is a storehouse: soil feeds, rocks shelter, and fossil fuels power, yet none are endless.

concepts.title: Conserving Nature's Treasures
concepts.definition: Treasures shrink when used carelessly, so conservation calls: use water twice, switch off lights, cycle short trips, plant trees, and turn to renewable energy such as wind and solar, in which India leads among nations.
concepts.key_idea: Saving a treasure is everyone's daily job: small acts, repeated by millions, keep nature's bank from running dry.
